key_insight: As layered perovskite oxides become thicker, their dynamical properties rapidly approach bulk behavior, supporting transferable model potentials.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-derived dynamical parameters could simplify modeling of layered oxide heterostructures, although the abstract does not evaluate solar-cell performance or AI methods.
method: Perform first-principles calculations on PbTiO3/SrTiO3 and ATiO3/AO superlattices and Ruddlesden–Popper phases.
Compare phonon densities of states and real-space interatomic force constants.
Assess convergence toward bulk dynamics as perovskite block thickness increases.
evidence_signal: Calculations across layered oxides with A = Sr, Ba, or Pb show rapid convergence toward bulk dynamical properties, but the abstract gives no numerical errors or convergence thresholds.
watch_item: Transferable potentials still require validation of interface-specific dynamics and accuracy across compositions and layer thicknesses.
paper_title: Lattice dynamical properties and interatomic force constants of transition metal oxide perovskite superlattices
